summary_md: Confidence stays at **opinion**. No evidence task has run, and the repo holds no outreach log or dated BridgeTrade notes (checked with Glob over `.bridgie/**`). Two evidence tasks are designed. E1, the real-model eval, is a data pull. E2, the external statement, is a document check plus a short past-behaviour interview. The panel's D1–D6 are folded into those two plus one cheap local test (E3, redaction survival) that needs no outside access. D7 is a scoping change, not an evidence task.

questions.context: E2 needs a named person who has run, or will run, a statement. I can't tell from the repo whether anyone has said yes in principle, and no outreach log exists to check. Who is the first interviewee and statement provider?
options: A named broker from the BridgeTrade conversations who has said yes in principle
A named lender analyst from a warm contact
Nobody yet: run the E2 interviews cold first, and start the week-6 clock only when someone agrees

questions.context: E2 and E3 involve a sole trader's statement, which is personal data even with the name removed. The owner chooses the data basis before any real statement is touched. Until then E3 runs on synthetic data only.
options: The lender anonymises on their side under their own basis, and we receive only the redacted file
Draft a short data-processing note and get a signed yes before receiving any file
Synthetic or self-generated statements only until the basis is settled

questions.context: E1 (real-model eval) spends tokens against the 20 USD appetite. Which model and how many runs per case is the owner's call. I propose 3 runs per case on one model, with a stop at 80% of budget.
options: One model, 1 run per case (cheaper, weaker on variance)
Two models, 1 run per case each

proposals.text: Keep v01-pilot-ready at **opinion** (tier definitions: opinion, anecdote 1–5 sources, data measured, test an experiment ran). Nothing has been measured or run. Raise to **data**, for the engineering claim only, once E1 publishes grounding rate and redraft counts from a real-model run. Raise to **test** only after E2 runs at least one statement redacted the way the lender would redact it, and the analyst's review is recorded. Even then, one statement supports 'ran once', not 'fit for pilots'. The demand claims (D1, D5, D6) stay at anecdote at best until 3 or more named sources are quoted.

E1 (data pull): run the existing eval suite against the chosen real model, 3 runs per case. Count numbers in each final memo that are absent from the metrics table (ungrounded) and count redrafts. Pre-register before running: pass = 0 ungrounded numbers in every final memo; the redraft count is reported but not gated. Stop rule: all cases done, or 80% of the 20 USD budget spent. Report the cases not run. Any ungrounded number is a blocker finding under kill criterion 1. Record the run id, model id and prompt hash in the artifact.

E3 (test, synthetic data, no outside access): redact the synthetic statement the way a lender plausibly would (names removed, then names plus account numbers removed). Run both through the pipeline and list which metrics survive, specifically M15 and the FPS CREDIT categoriser rules. Stop rule: two redaction variants, one run each. This answers D3's 'does the anonymised data still work' without a counterparty.

E2 (document check, then interview): (1) Document check first. Look for the dated BridgeTrade broker notes and an outreach log with names and dates. If they exist, quote them into the bet; this settles D1 and D5 without an interview. If they don't, say so in the bet and treat the problem quote as an assumption, the way lenders-will-pay already does. (2) Interview 3 to 5 analysts or brokers, stopping at 5 or at week 6, whichever comes first. Record each interview as its own source with date, role and quotes. Synthesis counts how many sources said each thing and quotes them; it does not average them.

Interview guide, past behaviour only, each question able to get a 'no'. (a) 'Think of the last memo you wrote from a bank statement. Walk me through it from the file arriving to sign-off. How long did each step take?' (b) 'In that file, what format did the statement arrive in, and who sent it? Can you show me a redacted example?' (settles D2). (c) 'When did a figure in a memo last turn out wrong? Who caught it and how?' (d) 'When did compliance, a funder or an auditor last ask where a number came from? What did you do?' (If it never happened, that is the finding.) (e) 'Have you tried an AI tool on memos or spreading in the last 12 months? What happened? If not, why not?' (settles D6). (f) 'Last time you wanted to try a new tool on live files, who had to say yes and what did they ask for?' (settles D3 and the budget owner). (g) For the pilot ask: 'Do you have a spread of an anonymised statement you could compare against, and what difference in a figure would you ignore?' (settles D4). Do not describe the product or show a demo before (a) to (f) are answered. Do not ask 'would you use / pay for this'.

D4 comparison method: one statement, with the analyst's existing spread as the baseline. Per metric, record: ours, theirs, and whether the analyst accepts the difference. 'Match' is the analyst's stated tolerance, taken before they see our numbers, not our choice afterwards. Report the matches, the mismatches and the unexplained, each as a count. 'Zero ungrounded' and 'matches the analyst' are separate results and are never merged into one pass.

D7: kill criterion 2 ('no lender or broker agrees by week 6') measures demand, which lenders-will-pay already owns with its own date (2026-12-19). Recommend v01-pilot-ready's kill criteria be: (1) a blocker in the money path that cannot be fixed in a week, as written; (2) E1 fails its pre-registered bar twice after fixes. Give the engineering fitness check a pass date of 2026-11-21, the end of the 2-week appetite. Move the lender-agrees condition to lenders-will-pay. The owner decides; I have only proposed it.

artifact_md:
# Evidence plan: v01-pilot-ready

Status 2026-11-07: **no evidence has been gathered**. Confidence is **opinion**. Searched `.bridgie/**` with Glob: there are no BridgeTrade notes and no outreach log in the repo. Anything said about them below is a thing to find, not a thing known.

## Method per task

| Task | Settles | Method | Sample | Stop rule | Resulting tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 real-model eval | engineering fitness, kill criterion 1 | data pull | full suite x 3 runs on one model | all cases done, or 80% of 20 USD | data |
| E3 redaction survival | D3 (data still works) | test on synthetic data | 2 redaction variants | both variants run once | test (synthetic only) |
| E2a notes and log check | D1, D5 | document check | the notes and log, or their absence | one search pass; record 'not found' as a result | none if missing |
| E2b interviews | D1, D2, D3, D4, D6 | interview, past behaviour | 3-5 people | 5 interviews or week 6 | anecdote (1-5 sources) |
| E2c external statement | D4, expected outcome | document check against analyst's spread | 1 statement minimum | analyst review recorded, or no statement received by week 6 | test (n=1) |

## E1 pre-registered bar

- Ungrounded number = any figure in a final memo that is not in that run's metrics table.
- Pass: 0 ungrounded numbers in every final memo, across all runs.
- Redrafts are counted and published, not gated.
- Report: model id, run date, cases and runs, ungrounded count, redraft count, cases not run and why.
- Limit: synthetic statements prove the pipeline works, not that it works on a lender's file.

## E3 redaction test

Run one synthetic statement three ways: original; payer names removed; names and account numbers removed. Table each metric as survives, degrades or breaks, with the reason. M15 and the FPS CREDIT categoriser rules are expected to break on payer-name removal. This is a hypothesis until the run shows it.

## Interview guide (past behaviour only)

Open with nothing about the product. Ask in this order:

1. Last memo you wrote from a bank statement: walk me through it from file arrival to sign-off, with times.
2. What format did the statement arrive in, and who sent it? Can you show a redacted example?
3. When did a figure in a memo last turn out wrong? Who found it, and what did it cost?
4. When did compliance, a funder or an auditor last ask where a number came from? What did you do? (Honest answer may be 'never'.)
5. Have you tried an AI tool on memos or spreading in the last 12 months? What happened? If not, why not?
6. The last time you tried a new tool on live files, who had to approve it, and what did they ask for?
7. Do you have a spread of an anonymised statement we could compare to? What difference in one figure would you ignore?

Show the product only after question 7, if at all. Do not ask 'would you' or 'how much would you pay'.

## Synthesis template (use once interviews exist)

For each question: number of sources who answered, number who gave each distinct answer, and verbatim quotes with source id and date. Mark 'never happened' answers as findings. No averaged conclusion. State the tier: 1-5 sources is anecdote and is labelled so.

## What would change the plan

- E1 finds any ungrounded number: fix, then rerun the full suite. A blocker that can't be fixed in a week triggers kill criterion 1.
- E3 shows the metrics break under redaction: the pilot as scoped can't run on redacted data, and the bet needs a different anonymisation method (agreed with the lender) or a changed scope.
- The interviews turn up a statement format other than the five-column CSV: that is an input to scope, since CAMT and MT940 adapters are a stated non-goal.

## Open owner decisions

See questions: first named contact, data basis for any real statement, E1 model and run count.
